source_text:
Epistula (e cod. Barocc. gr. 131)
Εὖ γέ σοι τῆς θαυμασίας ἐπιστολῆς· ὡς ἔαρος ἡμῖν προσέβαλε λογικοῦ, καὶ μουσικόν
τι λίαν ἀντὶ τῶν χελιδόνων ἠχεῖ. ὡς ἔνθους εἰμί τις ὑφ' ἡδονῆς, πάντα θαυμάζων,
τὴν λέξιν, τὸν νοῦν, τὴν ἁρμονίαν, τὸν γράψαντα.
orientation: Procopius is opening his letter by thanking the recipient for a letter that has delighted him.
pass_a_gloss: Well indeed for you for the wonderful letter; as it brought upon us a rational spring, and it sounds something very musical in place of the swallows. As I am someone inspired by pleasure, admiring everything, the wording, the thought, the harmony, the writer.

choices.term: Εὖ γέ σοι τῆς θαυμασίας ἐπιστολῆς
choices.english: Well indeed for you for the wonderful letter
choices.why: Keeps the exclamatory genitive of cause and the approving particle γέ, preserving the congratulatory force without smoothing it into a full sentence.
rejected: Well done to you for the wonderful letter
Good for you for the wonderful letter

choices.why: The compound προσβάλλω suggests an onset or arrival that strikes or comes upon, matching the spring's sudden arrival.
The present tense conveys an ongoing musical sounding, not a completed act.
The word means possessed or filled with a god, here transferred to the effect of pleasure; 'inspired' keeps the sense of being moved beyond oneself.
The prepositional phrase with genitive marks the agent or cause of the inspiration; keeping 'by' preserves the causal force.

pass_b_english: Well indeed for you, for your wonderful letter! It has brought upon us a rational spring, and in place of swallows it sounds something very musical. I am as one inspired by pleasure, admiring everything: the wording, the thought, the harmony, the writer.

problems.why: Same Greek phrase rendered differently; reader may think different states described.

problems.quote: I am as one transported by pleasure
problems.why: Same Greek phrase rendered differently; reader may think two distinct ideas are intended.
problems.fix: Use one rendering consistently across both versions.

variants.text: I am as one transported by pleasure
I am as one inspired by pleasure

edits.old: I am as one inspired by pleasure
edits.new: I am as one transported by pleasure

fixed: The English and literal gloss used different renderings of the same Greek phrase; the English now uses 'transported' consistently with the gloss.

problems.quote: It has brought upon us a rational spring
problems.why: Same sentence, different preposition across parallel sections.
problems.fix: Use one rendering consistently across all sections.

variants.text: It has brought us a rational spring
It has brought upon us a rational spring

edits.old: It has brought upon us a rational spring
edits.new: It has brought us a rational spring

fixed: Changed 'brought upon us' to 'brought us' for consistency with the parallel section's rendering of the same preposition.
